title: Phase B — mcpq CLI subcommands: list-tools, describe, call (typed args)
description:
## PROBLEM

Phase A shipped the foundation (protocol + transport + .mcpq.json + `mcpq servers`). The Phase B CLI subcommands `list-tools`, `describe`, and `call` are currently stubs that print "implemented in Phase B". This bead implements them with full ergonomic UX (human + json output) and the typed-args marshaling for `call`. Covers original beads xtrm-2m3.4 (read subcommands: list-tools, describe) and xtrm-2m3.5 (action subcommand: call with typed args).

## SUCCESS

Working subcommands end-to-end against the live sidecars on `mercury_platform`:
- `mcpq <server> list-tools` returns the live tool list (no hardcoded schema, fresh discovery every call). Human-readable default (table-ish) and `--json` raw output.
- `mcpq <server> describe <tool>` prints the input schema (typed args, required fields, defaults) plus tool title/description. `--json` flag supported.
- `mcpq <server> call <tool> [--arg key=value ...] [--json]` marshals typed args into a JSON-RPC `tools/call` payload, executes via MCPClient, renders the result. Type coercion: `key=value` defaults to string; `key:int=42`, `key:float=3.14`, `key:bool=true|false|1|0`, `key:json={"x":1}` for explicit typing.

End-to-end live proofs:
- `mcpq prometheus list-tools` returns 6 tools.
- `mcpq prometheus describe mercury_execute_query` shows schema with `query: string` (required) and optional `time` etc.
- `mcpq prometheus call mercury_execute_query --arg query='up{job="prometheus"}'` returns a vector result with at least one sample with `value=1`.
- `mcpq grafana list-tools` returns 49 tools.
- `mcpq grafana describe search_dashboards` shows input schema.
- `mcpq grafana call search_dashboards` returns ≥10 dashboards.

## SCOPE (MODIFY EXISTING + 1 NEW FILE)

**Existing files in `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/` — modify ONLY these:**
- `cli.py` — replace `_cmd_stub` calls for `list-tools`, `describe`, `call` with real implementations. Keep argparse subparsers as-is; wire them to new functions.
- `client.py` — minor: ensure `call_tool` returns a useful result envelope; add helper to convert `tools/list` result to the same shape regardless of server flavor.
- `protocol.py` — only if needed for `call_tool` envelope already exists in Phase A — likely no change.

**New file allowed:**
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/render.py` — output rendering helpers (human-readable tool list, schema pretty-printer, result rendering). Pure functions, no I/O. ~80 lines max.
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/args.py` — typed-arg parser for the `--arg key:type=value` syntax. Pure function `parse_args(items: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]`. ~50 lines max.

## NON_GOALS

- Tests (Phase D / xtrm-2m3.d).
- Skill body or expanded README beyond what already exists (Phase C).
- mercury-infra `.mcpq.json` integration (Phase D).
- stdio transport, multi-server batch, result caching.
- Schema validation against tool input schemas client-side (server is the validator; we just pass through).
- New third-party deps on the call path.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Python 3.10+ stdlib only on call path.
- Reuse Phase A `MCPClient` / `ServerSpec` / `validation` helpers — do NOT bypass `validate_url` / `validate_header_value` / `validate_container_name`.
- Telemetry MUST emit on every subcommand (success and error). Use `log_invocation(server, subcommand, tool, duration_ms, outcome)` — fill `tool` for describe/call, leave empty for list-tools.
- Human-readable output format hints:
  - `list-tools` default: one tool per line, `<name>  <title or description short>`, sorted alphabetically by name.
  - `describe` default: name, title, description, then `Args:` indented `  <field>  <type>  <required|optional> [default=<x>]  <description>`.
  - `call` default: pretty-print result (JSON with 2-space indent) — MCP `tools/call` results typically have `content: [{type: "text", text: "..."}]`; if so, print the joined text content; if not, fall back to full JSON.
- `--json` flag on all three subcommands emits raw JSON to stdout — no human formatting.
- Argument syntax for `call`:
  - `--arg name=value` → string
  - `--arg name:int=42` → int(value)
  - `--arg name:float=3.14` → float(value)
  - `--arg name:bool=true` → True (accept true/false/1/0/yes/no, case-insensitive); raises ValueError otherwise
  - `--arg name:json='{"x":1}'` → json.loads(value)
  - Raises clear error on type-conversion failure: "invalid value for arg <name> as <type>: <err>"
- Exit codes: 0 success, 1 user error (missing server, missing tool, bad args), 2 transport/server error.
- Errors go to stderr; telemetry one-line JSON also stderr (existing pattern). stdout for results only.

## VALIDATION

After implementation, in the executor worktree (it has the Phase A merged + the .venv-mcpq from prior):

1. `pip install -e packages/mcpq` clean.
2. `mcpq --help` shows all 4 subcommands (no "phase B stub" text).
3. From `packages/mcpq/`:
   - `mcpq prometheus list-tools` → paste full output (should list 6 mercury_-prefixed tools).
   - `mcpq prometheus list-tools --json | python3 -c "import sys,json; t=json.load(sys.stdin); print(len(t), 'tools'); print(t[0]['name'])"` → confirms json output is a list of tool dicts.
   - `mcpq prometheus describe mercury_execute_query` → paste output, must show `query` (string, required) at minimum.
   - `mcpq prometheus call mercury_health_check` → paste raw output (this is the safe no-arg call).
   - `mcpq prometheus call mercury_execute_query --arg query='up{job="prometheus"}'` → paste output; check it contains either result value=1 or a clear error explaining metric not exposed (label the outcome accordingly).
4. From `packages/mcpq/`:
   - `mcpq grafana list-tools` → paste tool count + first 5 names.
   - `mcpq grafana describe search_dashboards` → paste output.
   - `mcpq grafana call search_dashboards` → paste outcome (dashboard count if successful, or error if the grafana token lacks permission).
5. Telemetry: `mcpq prometheus list-tools 2>&1 1>/dev/null` → grep that telemetry JSON line contains `"server":"prometheus", "subcommand":"list-tools"`.
6. Error path: `mcpq prometheus call nonexistent_tool` → clear error message + nonzero exit code.
7. Argument typing: `mcpq prometheus call mercury_execute_range_query --arg query=up --arg start:int=1700000000 --arg end:int=1700000600 --arg step=15` → paste outcome (proves int coercion works).
8. Bad arg syntax: `mcpq prometheus call x --arg badform` → clear error.

## OUTPUT (handoff schema)

- Changed files list (modifications + new files)
- Pasted raw outputs for ALL VALIDATION steps 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8
- Confirm NO `.claude/`, `.codex/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` paths in `git show --name-only HEAD`
- Single clean commit on branch `feature/<bead-id>-executor`
- Branch force-pushed (origin set)
- Confirm telemetry still emits on EVERY subcommand
- Residual risks (e.g., behaviors not yet covered, server-specific quirks)
- Machine-readable block (as per per-turn handoff schema)

## REFERENCES

- Phase A shipped in 2ac44b4. The mcpq package is on main at packages/mcpq/. Self-test config at packages/mcpq/.mcpq.json. Phase A used .venv-mcpq at the worktree root.
- MCP spec tools/call: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/specification — request envelope `{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"<tool>","arguments":{...}}}`; response result envelope `{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"..."}], "isError":boolean}` or structuredContent for typed.
- Live sidecars on mercury_platform: infra-grafana-mcp (49 tools), infra-prometheus-mcp (6 mercury_* tools).
- Phase A noise filter: gitignore the executor's `.venv-mcpq`, `.smoke/`, `__pycache__/` and explicitly exclude any `.claude/` or `.codex/` paths from the commit.

title: Phase A — mcpq foundation: scaffold + protocol client + via-mode dispatch
description:
## PROBLEM

xtrm-2m3 epic requires a brand-new Python package at `~/dev/xtrm/packages/mcpq/` that bridges Docker-network-only MCP sidecars to host-side discovery and invocation. This bead covers the foundation: package scaffold (xtrm-2m3.1) + MCP protocol client with .mcpq.json discovery (xtrm-2m3.2) + via-mode dispatch supporting `host` and `docker:<container>` (xtrm-2m3.3). Without this foundation, no CLI surface or skill work can begin. The two live targets are `infra-grafana-mcp` (streamable-http :8090 on docker network `mercury_platform`, distroless image — no shell tooling inside) and `infra-prometheus-mcp` (http :8091 same network, has python3).

## SUCCESS

A working Python package at `packages/mcpq/` that: (a) installs with `pip install -e packages/mcpq` and exposes the `mcpq` console script on PATH; (b) reads `.mcpq.json` from the cwd or any parent dir; (c) performs the MCP streamable-http handshake (POST initialize → capture Mcp-Session-Id → notifications/initialized → tools/list / tools/call); (d) correctly parses both SSE-framed (`event: message\ndata: {...}`) and plain JSON responses; (e) supports two via modes: `host` (direct urllib from this process) and `docker:<container>` (shells out to `docker exec <container> python3 -c "<urllib script>"` reusing python3 in that container — NOT `curl`, since target sidecars are distroless). A trivial integration shows `mcpq prometheus list-tools` returns the 6 tools, executed via `docker:infra-prometheus-mcp`.

## SCOPE (NEW FILES ONLY — greenfield package)

- `packages/mcpq/pyproject.toml` — Python package metadata, console script entry point `mcpq = mcpq.cli:main`, no third-party deps for the call path. `python_requires = ">=3.10"`.
- `packages/mcpq/README.md` — minimal placeholder (Phase C will expand it)
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/__init__.py` — package marker with version
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/cli.py` — `main()` entry point only; argparse skeleton with subcommand stubs (only `servers` wired for Phase A smoke). Phases B add full subcommands.
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/config.py` — `.mcpq.json` discovery (walks up from cwd), schema dataclass for ServerSpec (`name, url, via, headers, transport`), loader returns `{name: ServerSpec}` dict.
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/protocol.py` — pure MCP protocol logic: build initialize / initialized / tools/list / tools/call JSON-RPC envelopes; SSE response parser handling both `event: message\ndata: {...}\n\n` and bare `{...}` shapes; session-id header capture (case-insensitive lookup of `Mcp-Session-Id`).
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/transport.py` — via-mode dispatch. Two backends: `HostTransport` (uses `urllib.request` directly) and `DockerTransport(container)` (runs `docker exec <container> python3 -c "..."` with a generated urllib script that performs the POST and prints response headers + body separated by sentinel). Both expose the same `post(url, headers, body) -> (status, response_headers, response_body_bytes)` interface.
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/client.py` — orchestrates protocol + transport: `MCPClient(spec).initialize() / list_tools() / call_tool(name, arguments)`. Maintains session-id across calls.
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/telemetry.py` — single function `log_invocation(server, subcommand, tool, duration_ms, outcome)` emits one-line JSON to stderr.
- `packages/mcpq/.mcpq.json` — example config pointing at the two live sidecars for self-test.

## NON_GOALS

- CLI subcommands `list-tools`, `describe`, `call` (those are Phase B / xtrm-2m3.b — only `servers` works after Phase A as a smoke).
- Skill body or expanded README (Phase C / xtrm-2m3.c).
- Tests (Phase D / xtrm-2m3.d) — DO NOT write tests in this phase except inline manual smoke proof in handoff.
- mercury-infra integration (Phase D / xtrm-2m3.d).
- stdio transport, multi-server batch, result caching, write variants.
- Any third-party dependency on the call path. Build / dev deps in pyproject `[project.optional-dependencies]` are OK if needed for Phase D test tooling, but the runtime call path is stdlib-only.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Python 3.10+ stdlib only on the call path (urllib, json, subprocess, argparse, dataclasses, pathlib, sys, os, time).
- The MCP protocol version negotiated must be `2024-11-05` or whatever the live sidecars advertise — read upstream MCP spec carefully (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/specification). Default to `2024-11-05`.
- Streamable-http handshake sequence (the spec calls this transport "Streamable HTTP"): POST `<url>` with body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{...}}` and Accept `application/json, text/event-stream`. Response will contain `Mcp-Session-Id` header (case-insensitive) — capture it. Body may be plain JSON or SSE-framed. Next, POST a `notifications/initialized` (no id) with the session header. Then `tools/list`. Then `tools/call`.
- SSE parser: split on `\n\n`, parse `event:` and `data:` lines, concatenate multi-line data, return the parsed JSON of the final `message` event. If body looks like raw JSON (`{` first non-whitespace), parse directly.
- Session-id header lookup MUST be case-insensitive. urllib `HTTPMessage` is case-insensitive by default; the docker-exec path returns headers as a dict — implement a small case-insensitive wrapper.
- `docker:<container>` transport: do NOT assume curl exists in the target container. The grafana sidecar is distroless. Strategy: serialize the urllib script as a single python `-c` argument; require the named container to have `python3` on PATH. Document this in README.md (Phase C). For the live verification step, use `docker:infra-prometheus-mcp` (it has python3 3.12) as the proxy for BOTH sidecars — the prometheus container is on the `mercury_platform` network and can reach both `http://infra-prometheus-mcp:8091` and `http://infra-grafana-mcp:8090` (and aliases `prometheus-mcp` / `grafana-mcp`).
- Telemetry MUST emit on every CLI invocation (success or fail). No payloads, no secrets, no headers. One-line JSON to stderr.
- No live network calls during package import. All HTTP only on demand.
- File layout `src/mcpq/` (PEP 517 src layout) so other xtrm packages have a clean convention to copy.
- `pyproject.toml` MUST use `setuptools` build-backend (stdlib-friendly, no poetry / hatch dependency just for one Python file's metadata).

## VALIDATION (must pass before handoff)

1. From repo root: `pip install -e packages/mcpq` succeeds in a venv (or `pip install --user -e packages/mcpq`).
2. `mcpq --help` prints subcommands (servers wired; list-tools/describe/call stubs print "implemented in Phase B" — do NOT implement them yet, but their argparse subparsers SHOULD exist so the help text is complete).
3. Create a self-test `.mcpq.json` at `packages/mcpq/.mcpq.json` pointing at both live sidecars via `docker:infra-prometheus-mcp`.
4. `cd packages/mcpq && mcpq servers` lists both `grafana` and `prometheus` configured servers with their `via` and `url`.
5. Smoke (run inside the worktree, after install): write a one-off Python script using the package internals to perform the full handshake against `prometheus` and call `list_tools()` — expect exactly 6 tools, all prefixed `mercury_`. Paste the script output (raw, untrimmed) in the handoff. This is the proof of working transport+protocol.
6. Run the same smoke for `grafana` (initialize + list_tools) — expect 40+ tools. Paste tool count and first 5 tool names in handoff.
7. Telemetry: `mcpq servers 2>&1 1>/dev/null | jq` must show one-line JSON with `server`, `subcommand`, `duration_ms`, `outcome` fields (server may be empty string for global `servers` cmd). Acceptable if `servers` emits zero telemetry (no remote call), but `list_tools` smokes MUST emit.

## OUTPUT (handoff schema)

- Changed files list (new only)
- pyproject.toml exact content
- Manual smoke proof: prometheus list_tools raw output + grafana list_tools raw output
- The `.mcpq.json` content used for the smoke
- Residual risks: e.g. SSE parser edge cases not yet covered, anything fragile about the docker-exec subprocess pipe
- Confirm NO code added for Phase B/C/D scope (subcommands beyond `servers`, README expansion, tests, mercury-infra .mcpq.json)
- ALL gitnexus impact analysis steps are N/A — package is greenfield, no existing symbols touched. Note this in handoff.

## REFERENCES

- MCP spec: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/specification (read protocol/transport/streamable-http section)
- Live sidecars on host: `docker ps --filter name=infra-` shows both; network = `mercury_platform`.
- Distroless grafana sidecar = NO curl, NO python3 inside grafana-mcp itself → must use a different network-attached container as the docker-exec proxy. `infra-prometheus-mcp` has `python3` at `/app/.venv/bin/python3` and is on `mercury_platform`.

SCRUTINY: high
close_reason: Phase A foundation shipped. mcpq package installable via pip install -e packages/mcpq; mcpq servers subcommand wired and emits telemetry; protocol+transport combo verified end-to-end against both live sidecars via docker:infra-prometheus-mcp proxy (prometheus: 6 mercury_* tools, grafana: 49 tools). Phase B stub subparsers in place.

title: mcpq — CLI + skill for querying Docker-sidecar MCP servers without .mcp.json bloat
description:
## PROBLEM

xtrm projects increasingly run OSS MCP servers (Grafana MCP, Prometheus MCP, future Loki/Tempo MCPs) as Docker sidecars on internal networks for substrate/specialist-agent use. Two problems with the obvious `.mcp.json` wiring path: (a) the sidecars are internal-only by design (no host port — defense in depth), so the host's Claude Code can't reach them at all; (b) even when host-reachable, loading 49+ tool schemas per session burns ~18k tokens of always-loaded context regardless of whether observability work happens that session. No existing CLI bridges this — `mcp-client`-style tools assume host-reachable URLs and stdio transport.

## SUCCESS

A `mcpq` CLI is installable from `~/dev/xtrm/packages/mcpq/` and available from any xtrm project. Subcommands: `mcpq servers`, `mcpq <name> list-tools`, `mcpq <name> describe <tool>`, `mcpq <name> call <tool> --arg key=val`. Tool catalog discovered live every call (no hard-coded schemas — image bumps don't break docs). A skill (`using-mcpq`) auto-loads when needed, teaches discovery, stays under ~150 lines regardless of server tool count. In mercury-infra, the two existing sidecars (`infra-grafana-mcp` 49 tools, `infra-prometheus-mcp` 6 tools) are reachable via `via: docker:<container>` indirection — no host port exposure.

## SCOPE

- New package: `~/dev/xtrm/packages/mcpq/` — first package in xtrm/packages/, establishes convention
- Per-project config: `<repo>/.mcpq.json` (CLI walks up cwd; mirrors `.mcp.json` discovery)
- Skill: `~/dev/xtrm/packages/mcpq/skills/using-mcpq/SKILL.md`
- Integration: `mercury-infra/.mcpq.json` referencing the existing two sidecars
- No changes to MCP sidecar deployment configs themselves

## NON_GOALS

- stdio transport (HTTP + streamable-http only in v1)
- Auth flows beyond static env-var injection at server-deploy time
- Multi-server batch calls or result caching
- Replacing `.mcp.json` for low-tool-count MCPs that benefit from native wiring
- A writable MCP variant (read-only is the design)

## CONSTRAINTS

- Python 3.10+ stdlib only (no third-party deps on the call path — trivial install)
- Per-server `via` field required; minimum two modes: `host` (direct urllib) and `docker:<container>` (exec into running Docker-network container; reuses its `curl`)
- SSE response framing must be parsed: handles both `event: message\ndata: {...}` and plain JSON shapes (different MCP servers use different framings)
- Session-id header matched case-insensitively (`Mcp-Session-Id` and `mcp-session-id` both seen)
- Tool catalog NEVER hard-coded — every list-tools/describe hits the server live
- Skill body capped ~150 lines; does NOT enumerate tools
- Telemetry: every invocation logs `{timestamp, server, subcommand, tool, duration_ms, outcome}` to stderr as one-line JSON; no payloads, no secrets

## VALIDATION

- [ ] \`mcpq prometheus call mercury_execute_query --arg query='up{job=\"prometheus\"}'\` returns vector with value=1 against running mercury-infra sidecars
- [ ] \`mcpq grafana call search_dashboards\` returns live dashboard list (≥10 entries)
- [ ] \`mcpq grafana describe search_dashboards\` prints input schema (typed args, required, defaults)
- [ ] \`mcpq grafana list-tools\` returns ≥40 tools (live count from sidecar at v0.15.2)
- [ ] \`mcpq prometheus list-tools\` returns exactly 6 tools (prom-mcp v1.6.1 with TOOL_PREFIX=mercury)
- [ ] Skill \`using-mcpq\` triggers on observability/MCP-query prompts; does not pre-load otherwise
- [ ] Smoke test gated on sidecars-up exists in tests/ and passes locally
- [ ] README.md documents install + per-project setup + the `via` semantics
- [ ] Telemetry jsonl observed on stderr for each invocation (greppable via \`mcpq ... 2>&1 | jq\`)

## OUTPUT

On epic close: link to merged PR(s), summary of CLI surface, verified mercury-infra invocations, cross-project portability notes (which other xtrm projects could adopt `.mcpq.json` now), and any drift findings discovered against the upstream sidecar images during test.

## REFERENCES

- mercury-infra session 2026-06-10 (infra-6if close-out) — context that motivated this epic
